findings.source_quote: οἷς ἔδει ἀποκαλυφθῆναι τὰ ὁράματα ταῦτα
findings.english_quote: to whom it was fitting that these visions should be revealed
findings.issue: The rendering reduces the obligation expressed by ἔδει to fitness or appropriateness. The lexical rationale explicitly acknowledges choosing wording softer than necessity, but supplies no passage-specific evidence warranting that reduction. The clause says these visions ought to have been revealed to the other, prior and better people; it does not merely describe them as suitable recipients.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “to whom these visions ought to have been revealed,” and revise the ἔδει lexical decision accordingly. This proposed replacement requires fresh review before acceptance.

findings.source_quote: οἷς ἔδει ἀποκαλυφθῆναι τὰ ὁράματα ταῦτα
findings.issue: The ἔδει lexical decision records this as the chosen rendering and explicitly justifies a softer force than necessity. That metadata does not describe the simplified text’s actual wording, “these visions should have been revealed to them,” which preserves the clause’s obligation. The inherited decision therefore misreports the translation and provides an unwarranted weakening rationale.
findings.suggested_revision: Update the lexical decision to record the actual “should have been” rendering and explain its preservation of the obligation expressed by ἔδει. Remove the unsupported softening rationale. Review the revised metadata afresh; this finding does not require weakening or replacing the current simplified clause.

summary: Both editions were checked independently against every clause of the selected Greek. Both retain the speakers, six builders, first-created angels, full creation assignment, completion promises, collective rejoicing, worthiness denial, past and future revelation, doubters’ positive-or-negative question, and all final truth assurances. The standard weakens ἔδει; the simplified text preserves its obligation but retains contradictory lexical metadata. The witness notes accord with the supplied bounded reports and distinguish corrections, mediated versions, preserved fragments, and editorial restorations without requiring a change to the working source. This review does not authenticate unseen images or certify an exhaustive collation. Servant and repentance terminology do not occur in this unit.
